articles.title: Michael Irvin rebukes Dak Prescott for an inappropriate comment: “He completely crossed the line”
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys legend was unimpressed by the veteran quarterback’s criticism of the home crowd in Arlington
articles.summary: The Cowboys legend was unimpressed by the veteran quarterback’s criticism of the home crowd in Arlington
articles.body:
M ichael Irvin has taken aim at Dak Prescott after the Dallas Cowboys quarterback criticized the atmosphere at AT&T Stadium following another disappointing defeat as the former wide receiver believes the player directed his frustration towards the wrong people after Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Dallas fell 46-40 in a game that exposed the team's defensive problems once again as San Francisco piled up 584 yards of offense, including 340 in the second half alone, whilst scoring 29 points after the interval to leave the Cowboys with another damaging result.

The defeat featured several embarrassing moments for the Dallas defense, including rookie Kaelon Black running through Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant on a 25-yard touchdown, whilst Deebo Samuel also broke free for a 70-yard score as Brock Purdy even contributing to blocks during the play.

Prescott , meanwhile, threw five touchdown passes and helped Dallas fight back from a 19-point deficit in a great performance from his side of things - however, when asked about having to use a silent count inside his own stadium, he turned his attention to the number of visiting supporters.

“[I] told myself early on that the red was for my high school,” Prescott said post-game. “All I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours.”

Those comments became a talking point on ESPN 's First Take on Monday, where Irvin delivered a blunt assessment as the three-time Super Bowl champion argued that Prescott should not have criticized the supporters, particularly when his remarks could be interpreted as speaking for the entire Cowboys fanbase.

“I certainly thought that he went in a direction that he should not have gone in his press conference,” Irvin said. “Talking about the number of people that were in the stadium, and that he was disappointed that the 49ers fans outstood the Cowboys fans.

“Like, you shouldn't be bewildered by that. You should not be baffled by that. He was speaking for a whole fanbase, and so when Dak gets on the podium and starts talking about the fans, I thought Dak Prescott was totally out of line.”

Defensive woes grow as Jones faces resignation calls

Irvin 's criticism came after a performance that intensified scrutiny of Dallas ' defense as the 49ers averaged an impressive 9.4 yards per play, rushed for 214 yards at 7.4 yards per carry and recorded the most offensive yardage ever conceded by the Cowboys in a home game.

Despite Prescott 's five touchdown passes as George Pickens caught three TD passes and finished with 145 receiving yards as Dallas narrowed the deficit to six points the defense could not prevent San Francisco from controlling the contest and Christian McCaffrey 's 66-yard touchdown reception ended the comeback.

The result left the Cowboys at 4-6, with their hopes of salvaging the season increasingly dependent on improvements across the team as Dallas still remains within reach of the NFC East leaders. However, the latest defensive collapse offered little reassurance that a turnaround is coming.

And pressure is also building around owner and general manager Jerry Jones as former NFL offensive lineman Richie Incognito had questioned his control of football operations before the 49ers game, arguing that Dallas needed an experienced general manager to oversee its roster decisions.

Dallas invested heavily in its personnel, bringing in Rashan Gary , Jalen Thompson , Durant , Dee Winters and Joey Porter Jr. , while selecting Downs and Malachi Lawrence . Yet the additions have not prevented opponents from repeatedly finding space against a defense that remains a major concern.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd tells Jerry Jones why his plan for the Cowboys is going to fall apart
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones faces growing pressure as Cowboys' locker room problems come under scrutiny
articles.summary: Jerry Jones faces growing pressure as Cowboys' locker room problems come under scrutiny
articles.body:
Colin Cowherd has delivered a blunt assessment of the Dallas Cowboys , and his warning to owner and general manager Jerry Jones goes beyond another disappointing result.

In the broadcaster’s view, it’s a team-wide failure of discipline that raises a much bigger question: do the players genuinely respect head coach Brian Schottenheimer ?

Dallas’ 46-40 home defeat to the San Francisco 49ers provided plenty of evidence for critics. San Francisco piled up an incredible 584 yards of offense, repeatedly finding ways through a defense that has struggled to contain opponents throughout the season.

Three touchdowns came on explosive plays of 74, 70 and 66 yards, making it another miserable afternoon for Dallas supporters at AT&T Stadium.

Cowherd believes the problems extend beyond defensive performances. He pointed to two recent disciplinary incidents involving DeMarvion Overshown and George Pickens . Overshown was penalized after running onto the field during the previous week's game, while Pickens received a taunting penalty against San Francisco.

According to Cowherd , these mistakes suggest players aren't worried about facing meaningful consequences from Schottenheimer .

“Cowboy players don't respect Brian Schottenheimer. They don't care. I mean, you can see it from the penalties, you can see it from the taunting, running on the field. And I mean, I'm just watching,” said Cowherd .

Jerry Jones could be approaching another major coaching decision

The statistics make the situation increasingly difficult to ignore. Through 10 games, Dallas ranked last in total defense, rushing defense and third-down defense, while sitting near the bottom of the league in scoring defense.

"They're on pace for their third straight losing season, and it's got very much a Dave Campo feel to it, where they don't do anything particularly well,” added Cowherd .

“Last in total defense, last in rush defense, last in third-down defense, next-to-last in scoring defense.”

That historical comparison could be particularly interesting for Jones . Campo's Cowboys went 5-11 in three consecutive seasons between 2000 and 2002. Eventually, the disastrous results prompted Jones to make a significant coaching appointment by bringing in Bill Parcells.

Although Parcells didn't deliver a Super Bowl championship, his arrival helped rebuild the roster and restored competitiveness.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys' current defensive struggles have raised questions about coordinator Christian Parker's future. Jones recently acknowledged that the organization is discussing potential changes to Parker's responsibilities following the embarrassing performance against San Francisco.

Schottenheimer has also confirmed that the coaching staff is reviewing the team's performances before deciding what adjustments might be necessary. Jones admitted that evaluating the defensive problems requires considering both coaching decisions and player performances.

However, changing Parker's responsibilities won't necessarily solve Cowherd's biggest concern. A defensive scheme can be adjusted, and coaches can be replaced, but neither decision automatically creates discipline or accountability inside the locker room.

Jones has previously defended the growing pains associated with hiring a young defensive coordinator and making significant personnel changes. Nevertheless, the Cowboys' latest setback puts additional pressure on the entire coaching structure.

articles.title: Jerry Jones is fed up with Cowboys and leaves door open for major coaching change
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys owner has seen his team's season go up in flames after yet another defensive disasterclass.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys owner has seen his team's season go up in flames after yet another defensive disasterclass.
articles.body:
The only reason Jerry Jones is still holding out hope for the Dallas Cowboys to make the playoffs is simply because the NFC East is having a down year. Even the first place New York Giants have shown a lot of flaws, even though they're ahead of the 4-6 Cowboys by a few games.

In any other year, the Cowboys would be considered fully dead right now. The past three weeks have featured a meltdown loss against the Arizona Cardinals , a four-point win against a decimated Indianapolis Colts team, and a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at home. That latest loss appears to be enough for changes to finally be made.

The Cowboys' defense has been the worst unit in the entire NFL this season, even though the front office focused almost all of their offseason moves on improving that side of the ball. Aside from the new players that were brought in, Jones and co. also fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and brought in rising young defensive coach Christian Parker from the Philadelphia Eagles .

Dallas Cowboys look ready to strip Christian Parker of playcalling duties

The 34-year-old Parker had never called plays before, so growing pains were expected. But Dallas' defense has seemingly regressed despite being historically bad last season . It sounds like Jones has had enough, as he finally admitted this week during his weekly local radio hit that head coach Brian Schottenheimer might have to take away Parker's playcalling duties .

" We are talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here. But we are talking about those things. "

Schottenheimer also refused to give Parker a vote of confidence after the loss to the Niners. It's becoming increasingly likely that someone other than Parker will be calling plays for the defense in Week 11 against the Tennessee Titans .
